contradicting_evidence: Only 26% of the selected Top-100 universe is advancing, and all observed alt capitalization proxies have negative mean and median 24h returns; this could extend into a more one-sided decline.
Price-down/OI-up conditions and negative final BTC and ETH ETF flows oppose assuming that a rebound will become recovery.
Stablecoin expansion remains undeployed in the supplied evidence, while favorable historical returns do not confirm current buying.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Two-way consolidation with downside retests and possible recovery attempts is more defensible than a continuous directional move. BTC may remain relatively firmer, while ETH and observed alt participation lag. Stabilization alone would not establish continuation; a durable upward path requires improving spot demand, ETH/BTC and participation together.
falsification_conditions: Persistent USD gains, stronger ETH/BTC and improving alt participation across successive observations would overturn the mixed path toward an upward trend.
Repeated failed recoveries followed by continued USD weakness, weak breadth and sustained demand deterioration would overturn it toward a downward trend.
New settled ETF sessions and spot-demand observations establish a consistent direction rather than the present conflicting signals.
missing_evidence: A multi-session price and breadth sequence showing whether participation survives retests.
ETF sessions after 2026-10-05 and repeated evidence of deployed liquidity.
Comparable ETH/BTC and BTC-dominance trends; isolated levels cannot establish rotation.
supporting_evidence: Current negative returns, weak participation and positioning vulnerability support retest risk, while positive BTC buying-pressure snapshots leave room for absorption and countertrend rebounds.
Stablecoin supply increased over 1d, 7d and 30d, providing potential liquidity support without confirming deployment.

The supplied 30d and 90d median alt returns are positive, with 53% and 59% outperforming BTC respectively. This historical participation limits a straight-line extrapolation of the weak 24h snapshot, but does not establish current transmission.
BTC's smaller 24h loss than ETH and the alt-proxy averages supports relative resilience rather than a broad-market recovery claim.
